question.text: In the context of mutual fund distribution, what does the term "B30 cities" refer to, and why is it significant?

answer.text: B30 refers to cities and towns beyond the top 30 locations in India, and SEBI permits additional commission/incentives for mobilising eligible investments from such locations as specified from time to time
B30 refers to the Bottom 30 performing mutual fund schemes that are allowed higher TER to cover losses
B30 refers to 30 benchmark indices, and funds tracking these indices get lower TER allowance
B30 refers to the first 30 business days of a scheme during which higher TER can be charged

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the NISM Series V-A workbook (pp.124, 127, 147), B30 stands for "Beyond Top 30" — these are cities and towns beyond the 30 largest locations in India. SEBI permits AMCs to offer additional commission/incentives for mobilising eligible investments from B30 locations, as specified from time to time, to promote geographical penetration of mutual funds. The Trap: B30 is a geographical classification — it is not about bottom-performing schemes, benchmark indices, or business days. It is also not tied to a single fixed "30 bps TER" figure; the additional commission/incentive structure is what SEBI specifies, and the specific quantum can change over time. Note: If you operate in a B30 city, eligible B30 inflows can attract additional incentives as specified by SEBI. This creates a real business opportunity for distributors in Tier 2/Tier 3 and smaller-town markets where mutual fund awareness is growing but penetration remains low.
